title: What is known about 1RB0RC_1LC0LD_1RA0LB_1LE0RA_1LB1LF_0LC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RC_1LC0LD_1RA0LB_1LE0RA_1LB1LF_0LC---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is a list of blocks (10)^n; the shift rules over blocks are proved in Lean, the block dynamics are only observed, and nothing found says whether the halting transition (F on a 1) can fire.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: Shift rules over the blocks
claims.text: Going right, A> (10)^n becomes (01)^n A> and C> (01)^n becomes (10)^n C>, each in 2n steps, for every n and every tape around.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 67,481 cells have been visited and 33,280 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.498). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.0).

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: tools/c/tmrun.c: 1010 steps from blank tape without a halt (114,618 ones).

claims.title: No closed tape language from windows up to 7
claims.text: bbtools.ctl with K = 2 to 6 closes but allows F to read a 1 (18 to 584 abstract halting configurations); at K = 7 it finds no closed set within its round limit; n-gram CPS (widths 3 to 7, -H, -U) fails.

claims.title: Blocks and fossils
claims.text: With the head in B at the left end the tape is (10)^n1 0 1 10 0 (10)^n2 0 1 10 0 …, blocks of 10 separated by 01100. The first block changes by one unit per round trip and the first few blocks trade units in long phases (the leftmost block fell from 3,644 to 3,636 in 8 round trips near step 3·109); the blocks further right repeat periodically (113, 369, 113, 369, …; 9, 41, 9, 41, …; 1, 1, 1, …), left there by earlier phases. The tape grows by about 2 cells per round trip at the left end (square root of the steps); the head reaches the right end only in rare phases (932 times in 9·108 steps), which is the logarithmic side.

claims.title: Where a halt would come from
claims.text: F is entered only from E reading a 1, after D read a 0, going left; in 109 steps (626,994 visits) F always read a 0, always with 11001 to its right and 01101 or 10101 (or the blank end) to its left. A halt needs D, moving left, to meet 1 1 0.

claims.title: Does it halt?
claims.text: Not known; the rule by which the first blocks trade units, and the rare phases that reach the right end, are not decoded.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 67,481 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.eyebrow: What the tape is made of
sections.heading: Blocks of 10, and fossils
html: Each time the head is at the left end in state B, the tape is a list of blocks of the word a = 10 separated by 0 1 a 0 (= 01100). At step 2,999,883,891 (width 116,432) it begins
The first few blocks are where the work happens; further right the blocks repeat periodically. They are fossils: each long phase of the left-end activity leaves a periodic stretch behind it.

sections.heading: A bouncer trading units between blocks
html: Going right, the head shifts each block it crosses by one cell (A> (10)^n → (01)^n A> and C> (01)^n → (10)^n C>, proved in Lean for every n). Each round trip changes the first blocks by about one unit and adds about 2 cells at the left end; in long phases a unit at a time moves from one block to another, as in the leftmost block shrinking from 3,644 to 3,636 over 8 round trips. Rarely, a phase carries the head all the way to the right end (the logarithmic side).

sections.heading: Only F on a 1
html: The only halt is F reading a 1. F is entered from E after D, moving left, has read a 0 and E a 1. In the first 109 steps F was entered 626,994 times and always found a 0, always with 11001 to its right. The question is whether the block dynamics can ever put a 1 1 0 in front of a left-moving D; it is open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.498). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.0).
After 109 steps the tape spans 67,481 cells (45,670 left of the start, 1,094 right), with a density of 1s of 0.493.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A list of blocks (10)^n separated by 01100: a bouncer at the left end moves units between the first few blocks and adds 2 cells per round trip, while older blocks further right stay as periodic fossils of earlier phases; the right end is visited only in rare phases.
